cells.tense: Right now the work is carrying on steadily, with hands that know the ground they are working.
cells.act: go on toward it without needing a sign
cells.ask: Pick the thing you are bringing along and keep at it this week on the ordinary days, without watching for proof it is working — just the next small stretch, done because you chose it.
cells.core:
You are holding the work steady while it presses on you, and none of it is loud — the strength sits in what you carry when nobody is watching. Here it looks like patience with something still small: you keep the conditions right and let time do its part, so the growing is neither forced nor dropped. Care with a spine in it.

The way through this week is continuing without needing proof. Choose the thing you are bringing along — a person, a piece of work, your own body in a routine — and tend it on the plain days when nothing answers back. Going on is the method. You are not waiting for a sign to keep going; you are going, and a sign would be welcome but is not required.
cells.sheetLine: You keep going without needing a sign, and that is the strength.
cells.verb: holding steady through what presses on you, from the inside
cells.place: the patch of soil where something is being brought along, with time and patience

cells.tense: By next week the whole future of the growing thing will have to be settled in advance.
cells.act: give one thing and take one thing, in balance
cells.ask: With someone close to this, say plainly what you are carrying and hear what they carry — then put down a piece that was not yours, and take up a piece they offer.
cells.core:
The care has outrun what is being cared for. You are trying to guarantee the outcome before it has had a chance to unfold, and tending has turned into managing — checking, arranging, holding what was not yours to hold. It looks like strength and feels like strain, and what is under your hands can tell the difference.

The correction is exchange at its true size. Say what you are carrying to someone close to this — a partner, a friend, a coworker — and hear theirs. Then put down the piece that belongs to them, and accept a piece back. Even helping runs both ways when it is healthy. Hold without forcing this week, and let someone else hold a piece.

cells.tense: What you hand over has gone to where nobody was watching, and it has stayed there.
cells.act: do the giving in the open this time, where it was always done unseen
cells.ask: Do the next stretch of caring where the one it is for can see you — unannounced, in front of them, no explanation afterward — and notice what it costs to be watched while you do it.
cells.core:
You are past a door you already walked through, and your hands keep working while the effort goes somewhere nobody looks. Because it happens unseen, it cannot be met, and caring that was strength has thinned into upkeep. What you carry is real; nothing comes back that says it counted.

Let one visible piece be done where the one it is for can see you — the next stretch, in front of them, no explanation afterward. Being seen is what refills this. If acknowledgment comes, take it. Your strength was not in staying invisible; it was in keeping at the work, which is real whether or not anyone named it.

cells.tense: You keep going quietly past what it has cost, and your own account does not mention the going.
cells.act: persist on hope that has been tested
cells.ask: Keep after something you are still reaching for after everything — a small step this week, full knowledge of how hard it has been, and no waiting to feel encouraged.
cells.core:
There is a hopefulness running this that you do not count as hopefulness. Your words for it are getting on, keeping things going, being realistic — and meanwhile you keep reaching toward something through stretches that have already tested you. The record shows it in what you keep doing; the way you describe it leaves the strength out. The one who keeps this going is missing from your own story.

The turn is to keep after a hope that has been tested. Pick the thing you are still reaching for after everything, name it plainly to yourself, and take a small step toward it this week without waiting to feel encouraged. You do not need a fresh sign. The sign already happened: you are still going.
cells.sheetLine: You keep going on hope you would not call hope.
cells.verb: holding steady through what presses on you, from the inside

attempts.check: The refused draft slipped in three habits I have to break: turning the working verbs into nouns ('the tending,' 'the carrying,' 'the steadiness') so they sound grave, and using 'never' where the record only claims one capacity in one part of a life. The Too Little cell also supplied a duration the person never gave, and named the medicine as if it were a character; the fix is to keep the stance ('still at the door,' giving done where nobody watched) and strip the history. The reader's likely objection is that the Balanced cell flatters quiet persistence, so the core names what is actually happening — strength drawn from what is carried, no audience — rather than praising it. All four asks survive being wrong: each is a small, visible, doable act (going on without proof, evening an exchange, letting one piece be seen, keeping after a tested hope), useful whether or not the signature fits. The line that serves me more than the person is the Too Little 'the giving went on where nobody watched,' which edges toward a story I do not have.
